geometry_edits.rationale: Align the notch with the verified frontage/access side.
Widen the public cut to make the access edge read as a real void.
Raise the notch to strengthen the entry seam and ground publicness.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent dominant mass in all four views, with a recognizable cross-like plan and a unified carved/notched top, so gesture clarity and hierarchy are solid. It also appears to respect the parcel boundary rather than merely filling the box. However, the form remains mostly a compact extruded object with faceted edges; the stepped upper silhouette is not strongly capacity-bearing or sectional in a way that clearly supports neighborhood living. The blue frontage edge is acknowledged only weakly: there is some offset/entry articulation, but the street response is not yet a robust public void or active threshold. Overall the mass is plausible for neighborhood mixed-use, but it needs a stronger ground-level court/notch and more legible access-oriented void to better align with the semantic brief.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is much larger and more campus-like than the candidate; transfer the courtyard/terrace principle, not the multi-building tower composition.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Perimeter-courtyard campus logic with stepped/terraced low-rise massing and a clear communal center can support neighborhood-scale public life.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is taller and more monolithic; avoid copying the single-story pavilion typology or ornamental frontage.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact, low-rise pavilion can establish a readable street edge with a simple entry setback and attached vertical/service marker.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is a counterfactual of a housing typology with a stronger sectional terrace logic than the candidate; useful only as a sectional operation reference.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A continuous stepped/courtyard section can create inhabitable terraces and a legible upper-lower hierarchy.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied from the visible frames; no hard-gate failure detected.
The primary access edge is only lightly engaged; the ground response could be more explicit and public.
The stepped upper profile reads more as a graphic silhouette than as program-bearing section.
No view-coherence collision issue is apparent; the mass remains legible across all views.
